title: Tahirid Sultanate
capsule: The Tahirid Sultanate of Yemen was founded by 'Amir ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Tahir in 1454, succeeding the Rasulid dynasty as the dominant power in the Yemeni lowlands and establishing its capital at Rada'. The sultanate controlled the Tihama coast, the fertile middle highlands, and significant Red Sea trade routes, and at its height in the late fifteenth century exercised nominal suzerainty over much of Yemen. The Mamluk sultanate of Egypt, seeking to counter Portuguese incursions into the Indian Ocean spice trade, sent an expedition to Yemen in 1516–1517 that destroyed Tahirid power; the sultanate was extinguished when 'Amir ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab was killed and his domains absorbed by Mamluk and subsequently Ottoman forces.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Tahirid territorial extent is broadly described in medieval Arabic chronicles, but detailed mapping of their control in the highland interior versus lowland coast is based on inference from partial administrative sources.
